# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction labeling logic.

Routes (`Controller.py`):
- `GET /` → `{"response": "Hello! Flask."}` (line 51-53)
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` (line 55-67) — payload `{transactions:[...], accountUID}`
- `POST /categorizeTransaction` (line 69-936) — payload `{bank, acc_type, accountUID, accountHolder, isPFMEnabled, transactions:[...]}`

Input transaction columns consumed by the code: `description`, `remark`, `type` (`"CREDIT"`/`"DEBIT"`), `amount`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `transactionDate` (`%d/%m/%Y`). Output columns added: `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2`, `isInternalPayment`, optionally `pfmCategoryOne/Two/Type`, `pfmSimpleDescription`, `Group_ID`.

A recommended test entry point (nothing exists yet) is to call the pure functions directly, e.g. `categorize_HDFC_transactions(df, "SAVING")` then `purpose(...)` then `clean_names(...)` — they are all plain `DataFrame -> DataFrame`.

Key semantics to know when writing tests:
- `sep_by_(s, n1, n2)` = "take slash-separated tokens `[n1:n2)` and re-join **with empty string**" (so a 2-token slice loses the delimiter, e.g. `sep_by_dash(d,2,4)` glues token2+token3).

- Every rule table is evaluated by `np.select(conditions, choices, default=...)` → **first matching row wins**, so rule order is semantically significant everywhere.

steps.message:
Found and fixed five faults, all boundary/offset errors inside otherwise-correct rules.

## Fixes

**1. Cheque deposit from an all-numeric reference note** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`
The rule required `remark` length `== 15` while the regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 characters, so it could never fire and the row fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Changed to `.eq(16)` (consistent with the 16-digit remark rules at HDFC.py:214-215).

**2. Salary sub-tag on a bare numeric narration** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`
Guard compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`; the controller and every other rule in the codebase use `"SAVING"` (`Controller.py:106` etc.). The rule was dead. Changed to `"SAVING"`.

**3. Counterparty on direction-keyword narrations** — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`
`py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` lifted group 0 — the direction word — instead of the name. `"To"` was then wiped by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` cleanup (empty name), `"From"` survived as the payee (wrong name), matching the report exactly. Changed to `index=1`.

**4. Slash-delimited bill reference, four fields** — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`
For `^BIL/INFT/` with exactly 3 slashes (type / sub-type / numeric ref / payee) the rule took token 2 (the numeric ref), which was later scrubbed by the `[0-9]{6,}` filter, leaving no payee. Changed to `sep_by_(description, 3, 4)` — the final field — consistent with the 5-field rule on the next line.

**5. Offsetting credit recorded as a bounce** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`
The REVERSAL rule compared `description.eq(description.shift(2))` while checking the type/amount of the *immediately preceding* row, so a matching debit/credit pair never satisfied it and dropped into the `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rule below. Changed to `shift(1)`.

## Verification

Reproduced each case from a single synthetic row before the change, confirmed the corrected label after, then ran a 34-row HDFC and 20-row ICICI corpus (UPI, IMPS, NEFT/RTGS, POS, ATM, cheque, ACH/SI, refunds, reversals, BIL/INF/MMT slash forms, both `SAVING` and `CURRENT`) through the full `categorize → purpose → clean_names` pipeline against the pre-change code. The diff contains only the five reported situations; every other row's category, sub-category, merchantType and partyName are byte-identical.

One knock-on worth flagging: the row in case 1 now correctly labels `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, and as a result HDFC.py:215 (which only applies to `TRANSFER` rows with a 16-digit remark) no longer copies the narration into `partyName`, so that row's name is blank. That is the original pre-fault behaviour of this rule pair, not a new regression, but it means these cheque rows carry a category without a payee unless one of the `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*` forms matches.
